newsitem.title: CANADA: Thomson mum on sale of U.K. leisure unit.
newsitem.headline: Thomson mum on sale of U.K. leisure unit.

text.p: Thomson Corp declined to comment on Monday on published reports in Britain that the company was looking to sell its U.K.-based leisure unit, Thomson Travel Group, to London investment banks.

A spokesman at Thomson's Stamford, Connecticut headquarters declined to confirm that the Toronto-based conglomerate was in talks to sell the travel unit, which comprises Britain's second largest charter airline and the Lunn Poly chain of travel agencies.
In 1996, Thomson Travel accounted for US$2.48 billion, or 33 percent, of the conglomerate's US$7.72 billion in revenue.

Thomson's major holdings include the travel group, Thomson newspapers, which publishes more than 100 daily newspapers in North America and more than 350 advertising supplements, and West Publishing Co, acquired by Thomson in 1996 for US$3.425 billion in cash.
